A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same study, with comparable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D. Layout changes and renumbering do not prevent matching the content.

before.justification: v1 reports original grid-world and Overcooked-AI simulations, human-behavior prediction results in Table 1, and human-subject evaluations in Figure 8.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulations, human-behavior prediction results, and human-subject evaluations, including Table 1 and Figure 7.

M1.justification: The CNN predictor, Lagrangian objective, discrete gradient optimization, and learned human-behavior model remain unchanged. Revisions concern experimental constraints and reporting rather than a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate grid-world navigation, single-agent Overcooked-AI, optimal and hyperbolically discounted behavior, and human navigation. The same task and population coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain exhaustive search, Pruned-Reduce, greedy search with true or predicted wcd, and the same human-study treatments. Initial is renamed Original; comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated Overcooked design space changes from adding, removing, or relocating objects to relocation subject to reachability. The human-overlap calculation is redescribed from averaging paths and varying observed fractions to reporting a distribution through percentiles. These are reported protocol revisions, without establishing that experiments were rerun; sample counts and splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing human-study comparison of optimal versus learned behavior models receives revised overlap-distribution summaries and inference results in v2 Figure 7 versus v1 Figure 8. This revises evidence about the learned behavior model's contribution without adding an ablation factor or robustness scenario.

E5.justification: The overlap plot changes from curves with error bars and shaded bands in v1 Figure 8a to grouped bars without those uncertainty displays in v2 Figure 7a. Other plots retain uncertainty markers; neither version explains their statistical construction or reports repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Several central comparisons change. Figure 6's proposed-method plateau rises from approximately 2.5 to 3.2 wcd reduction under the retained stated setting. Human inference curves change, including a 100% endpoint for every treatment in v2 Figure 7b. Overcooked results are replaced alongside revised reported constraints; v2 Figure 9d now places predicted-wcd greedy search ahead of the proposed method in runtime at larger budgets. Table 1 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: The MDP and behavioral-policy definitions, discounting functions, wcd formulation, constrained objective, and Lagrangian remain equivalent. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit claim that this is the first work to evaluate goal-recognition environment design through human-subject experiments. The main claims about flexibility, effectiveness, and runtime efficiency otherwise remain.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly states the assumption that user behavior remains static and explicitly identifies static, fully observable environments as limitations. It also adds privacy and surveillance implications. Dynamic and partially observable environments were already discussed as future work in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds hardware specifications in Appendix A.2, defines the Overcooked budget through total Manhattan displacement in B.1, and explains masking the alternative human-study goal in D. These are new disclosures. Conversely, it removes the named MLP tuning parameters—learning rate, hidden-layer size, and L2 penalty—from Section 5.2.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tang and Ho's 2019 and 2021 works and Feng, Ho, and Tang's 2024 work, broadening discussion of human behavior in computational systems. It also adds the human-experiment novelty claim. Most positioning and cited literature remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, human-overlap discussion, and conclusion receive localized rewrites. Subsection numbering, acknowledgements, and a budget subsection are added, while the overall narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: The paper is comprehensively reformatted from two columns to one. Figure 1's panels become horizontal, Table 1 is transposed, Figure 2's grid example changes, and human-overlap curves become grouped bars. Interface illustrations are consolidated in the appendix, with extensive figure resizing and relocation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through budget, hardware, interface, and limitation disclosures, and corrects v1's confusing overlap-analysis description. However, its revised Overcooked runtime plot in Figure 9d contradicts Section 5.1.3's retained claim of being at least three times faster than predicted-wcd greedy search. The human-overlap display also loses uncertainty information, and several numerical revisions remain unexplained. These substantive benefits and reporting problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
